new_packages.label: רוּחַ שְׁטוּת וּמֶלֶךְ זָקֵן וּכְסִיל
new_packages.label_en: Spirit of Folly and the Old Foolish King
new_packages.reason: The Torah explicitly presents an evil structural mirror to the main מלכות/שכינה/רוח הקדש cluster. The evil cluster is built around three bechina-connected concepts found in the source text: (1) מלך זקן וכסיל — the 'old foolish king,' which is the evil counterpart to מלכות דקדושה. Attaching to it is the definition of wickedness ('דבוק אל מלך זקן וכסיל'). (2) רוח שטות — the spirit of folly, which is the exact evil mirror of רוח הקדש. The Talmud (Sotah 3a) says 'אין אדם עובר עברה אלא אם כן נכנס בו רוח שטות.' This is the anti-ruach-hakodesh. (3) רשעים/מתים בחייהם — the wicked, who 'in their lifetime are called dead' because they are disconnected from the holy Malkhut and draw from the spirit of folly instead. The text explicitly draws the structural parallel: 'אבל להפך, נכנס בו רוח שטות' — the wicked draw rуach shтut just as the righteous draw ruach hakodesh. This mirror structure is a defining feature of Rebbe Nachman's teachings and is confirmed by the framework document (section 4). The three evil concepts (מלך זקן וכסיל, רוח שטות, רשעים בחייהם קרויים מתים) share the essential nature of disconnection from Malkhut/Kedushah — the anti-Shekhinah domain.

proposed_nodes.source_quote: שׁוֹאֵב רוּחַ שֶׁל שְׁטוּת, כִּי דָּבוּק אֶל מֶלֶךְ זָקֵן וּכְסִיל (קהלת ד')
אֵין אָדָם עוֹבֵר עֲבֵרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת. אֲבָל לְהֵפֶךְ, נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
רְשָׁעִים בְּחַיֵּיהֶם קְרוּיִים מֵתִים (ברכות יח:), כִּי מֵחֲמַת שֶׁנִּפְסָק מֵחֶבֶל דִּקְדֻשָּׁה, מֵאַיִן יִהְיֶה לוֹ חִיּוּת

new_packages.mirror_explanation: This evil package mirrors Package 1 (מלכות ושכינה) precisely: מלך זקן וכסיל mirrors מלכות דקדושה; רוח שטות mirrors רוח הקדש; רשעים/מתים mirror the concept of תחיה (resurrection/life). The same structural axis — a king, a spirit, and a state of life vs. death — appears on both the good and evil sides. The bechina language in the source text makes these equivalences explicit.

observations: Torah #78 presents a tight, unified teaching about the nature of Malkhut/Shekhinah as the root of all holiness — speech, Ruach HaKodesh, the spirit of Mashiach, the divine union, and resurrection all share one essential nature. The evil mirror is equally clear but entirely absent from the current dataset. The text explicitly states the anti-structure: the wicked are disconnected from holy Malkhut, attach to the 'old foolish king,' absorb a spirit of folly (the inverse of Ruach HaKodesh), and are therefore considered dead even in their lifetimes. This is a textbook good/evil mirror structure per the framework document (section 4). The editorial note at the end of the Torah (§21) acknowledges that the text is not fully organized and lacks some content ('אינם מסודרים יפה וחסר בהם גם כן'), which explains the relatively sparse dataset (11 bechina edges, 13 nodes). The evil mirror package is supported by at least 3 independent concepts with explicit bechina-language relationships in the source text and qualifies for a new package proposal. Additionally, the Torah's section on the two types of burning (§§25-28) — holy burning toward God vs. burning toward worldly desires — may represent a third domain (neutral/structural) describing the mechanism of spiritual intensity, but it lacks explicit bechina language connecting its nodes and is likely better represented as an eitza framework. No new package is proposed for it.
